correctness.rationale: For every fixed alpha>0 and d>=2 the infinite-past linear equation gives the exactly normalized independent Beta(1,alpha) GEM weights and uniform sphere directions. Pairwise sphere-dot covariance proves E[Q|P]=S and Var(Q|P)=2(S^2-T)/d; explicit Beta moment recursions give the exact error, mean, variance and fourth-power-sum coefficients. Finite-K multivariate Lindeberg CLT for independent Gaussian coordinate products gives independent Gaussian coordinate and pair-dot limits; uniform-in-d conditional L2 tail bounds permit K→infinity and yield the two-component stable conditional limit. The variance of Simpson S is strictly positive. Finite exact arithmetic and independent Monte Carlo checks from verify.py passed 123 assertions; these are corroboration, not substitutes for the proof. Limitations are athermal stationary isotropic Poisson-refresh dynamics with dimension-independent positive rates.

value.rationale: The physically motivated d-dimensional harmonic run-and-tumble model provides a nontrivial example where the norm of a high-d stationary trajectory does not self-average despite independent asymptotically orthogonal propulsion orientations. A random Simpson-index radius survives due to persistent renewal intervals; the exact 1/d radial mean-square error and conditionally independent radial/coordinate Gaussian noise specify observable fluctuation scales. The non-Gaussian Cartesian variance mixture gives a falsifiable cross-dimensional diagnostic. This is a structural quantitative limit theorem, not a parameter rename, textbook moment or arbitrary sample-size extension; finite-dimensional kurtosis is only a supportive known-derivable diagnostic.
